title: Deployment cadence taktboard and release digest (Sep 2026) - draft
content:
Summary:
This doc is a working taktboard for the Sep 2026 deployment campaign. Purpose: give a compact, cadence-driven checklist + hour-by-hour day-of schedule, clear signal gates for progressive exposure, and a short user-facing release digest draft. Use-case: medium-risk runtime changes (kernel selector update + small batching policy tweak) landing to hosted and Dedicated fleets.

High-level campaign concept (taktboard language):
- Pulse window: tight, frequent verification steps (0-4 hours post-deploy)
- Drift window: broader traffic expansion and cost observation (4-24 hours)
- Settle window: full traffic, 72 hour monitoring for regressions

Preflight checklist (must be green before staging go/no-go):
- Configuration and code:
  - Model pin manifest created and committed (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1203).
  - Kernel selector flags tied to feature flag `ff.runtime.kernel-v2` with safe default off.
  - Batching policy change (reduce max_batch_latency from 20ms to 12ms) documented and smoke-tested locally.
- Infra & infra-owner tasks:
  - Dedicated capacity reserve validated for Sep 10-12 (capacity ticket REL-7921).
  - Canary fleet tagged with `canary-sep-2026` images; image hash verified.
  - KMS rotation check: customer key access validated for Private customers (run kms-check v2).
- Observability & telemetry:
  - Dashboards created: `release/sep-2026/latency-p95`, `release/sep-2026/error-rate`, `release/sep-2026/cost-per-token`.
  - Synthetic smoke suite: `smoke/small-inputs` and `smoke/long-context` pass locally and on staging.
  - Regression eval set run (20 prompts) with divergence metric < 0.015 compared to baseline model.
- Runbook & comms:
  - Release notes draft ready (see below).
  - Oncall rotation locked and paging policy confirmed (pager escalation to SRE lead Marcus Lee).
  - Stakeholder brief sent to product + cs + legal.

Staging verification script (to run after staging deploy):
- Run synthetic smoke (5 iterations) — assert p99 < 1.2x baseline and p95 delta < 50ms.
- Run 20-regression prompts — target token-difference < threshold.
- Run KV-cache warm-up: replay 500 historical requests to validate cache behaviour.
- Confirm metrics emit: token_count, kernel_selection, batching_latency, kv_hits.
- Manual exploratory: sample 10 streaming responses for truncation or decoding artifacts.

Canary schedule (progressive exposure) - day-of timeline (hours relative to canary activation):
- T+0min: promote canary images to `canary-sep-2026` namespace; route 0.5% traffic. Begin Pulse window.
- T+15m: check health endpoints across 10% of canary pods; quick smoke run.
- T+30m: if no regressions, increase to 2% traffic.
- T+90m: evaluate metrics; if stable, 10% traffic. Run expanded regression eval (100 prompts).
- T+4h: move to Drift window — 25% traffic. Conduct cost sampling across 10k requests.
- T+12h: if telemetry is green, 50% traffic and initiate Dedicated pool validation (limited to non-customer-critical pools).
- T+24h: if no regressions, 100% traffic for hosted API; Dedicated to be scheduled by ops according to customer impact matrix.
- T+72h: Settle window complete. Nightly synthetic run and final verification.

Signal gates (explicit abort conditions):
- Abort and automatic rollback if any of the following in the Pulse or Drift windows:
  - p95 latency increase > 40% vs baseline for two consecutive 15m windows.
  - error rate > 1% absolute increase over baseline for 30m.
  - model divergence metric > 0.03 on regression eval.
  - KV-cache hit-rate drop > 25% for 30m.
  - any critical customer-facing incident reported via CS within pulse window.

Rollback & mitigations plan (fast paths):
- Automated rollback via orchestration command: `relctl rollback --campaign sep-2026 --to-prev` (ops team).
- If rollback fails, scale down canary pods, revert traffic routing, and trigger hotfix branch creation.
- Communication: send Slack template to #release-campaigns and tag stakeholders (product, SRE, CS).

Day-of quick-play checklist (hour-by-hour compact):
- -60 to 0 min: preflight sign-off (all green indicators), staging verifications completed.
- T+0: promote canary, route 0.5%, start 15m watch.
- T+15: short sync (channel pinned) — report initial smoke results.
- T+30: expand to 2% if green.
- T+90: 10%, run expand eval.
- T+240: 25%, run cost-sample (billing snapshot).
- T+720: 50%, Dedicated validation.
- T+1440: 100% hosted traffic. Day owners: Priya (release lead), Marcus (oncall SRE), Elena (observability), Sam (customer comms).

Telemetry & SLOs to watch (primary):
- Latency p50/p95/p99 per model and per route.
- Token throughput and estimated cost-per-1k-tokens.
- Request error rate (4xx, 5xx) by code and by region.
- Kernel selection distribution and rare-path fallback counts.
- KV-cache hit ratio and cache size percentiles.
- Regression score drift against curated eval set.

Post-deploy tasks (first 72 hours):
- Nightly automated regression run and report to #release-digest.
- Ops to run cost sampling job and compare against forecast; if cost > 20% projected, open REL-cost-review.
- CS to collect top 10 customer feedback items and escalate criticals.
- Retrospective: schedule 1-week + 30-day retro with owners and triage list.

Draft release notes (user-facing, editable):
Title: Small runtime and batching efficiency update — Sep 2026
Short blurb: Today we rolled out an optimization that improves throughput and reduces transient latency for short-request workloads. This update adjusts the kernel selection heuristics and reduces inference batching latency to deliver snappier responses for many API calls.
What changed (technical):
- Kernel selector: better heuristics to pick quantized kernels for shorter contexts.
- Batching latency policy: reduced max buffering window for short requests, lowering median latency at the cost of slightly reduced batching efficiency on some heavy-batching workloads.
- Observability: new dashboard surfaces kernel selection counts and per-route token cost.
Impact and guidance for customers:
- Most workloads will see lower median latency with similar accuracy.
- If you observe increased cost for high-throughput batch-heavy endpoints, contact support to discuss tailored batching profiles or pin to previous runtime.
- Dedicated/private customers: we will schedule separate maintenance windows for any on-prem changes; contact your account team for details.
Known issues and caveats (so far):
- Very long-context batch-heavy jobs may see a small throughput regression in rare cases — tracking under REL-7934.
- Some quantized model variants may select fallback kernels under edge conditions; we have mitigations in the pipeline.

Open questions / TODOs (short list):
- Decide default canary retention window for Dedicated: 24h vs 72h. (Assigned: Priya).
- Finalize cost-sample thresholds and set automatic alerting. (Assigned: Elena).
- Confirm whether `ff.runtime.kernel-v2` should be enabled by default for staging. (Assigned: Marcus).

Appendix: quick links and commands
- relctl status --campaign sep-2026
- Dashboard: observability/release/sep-2026 (Confluence link in metadata)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1203
- Incident channel template: /compose @here "Sep-2026 campaign: aborting, reason=..."

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this page minimal; heavier notes to go into Confluence campaign doc after postmortem.
- Watch for spike patterns on region eu-west1 — historical 3x variance during kernel selector changes.
- If we hit rollback, collect request traces for 15m before rollback to attach to REL ticket.

Last updated by: Priya Kapoor (2026-09-08).
